issues.legal_issue: A finding of possession in a suit for injunction may be disturbed in second appeal when it is vitiated by the failure to consider vital documentary evidence.
material_facts: The suits sought permanent injunctions based on claimed possession of agricultural land.
The lower courts found in favour of the appellant on possession, relying on oral evidence.
Documents recording a compromise and surrender of possession, and revenue-court orders dismissing proceedings on the basis of the compromise, had not been considered.
The High Court reconsidered the evidence and disturbed the possession finding; the Supreme Court found no infirmity in the High Court’s assessment.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in interfering with the possession finding because vital documents had been ignored; the appeals challenging that decision were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A factual finding in a second appeal may be interfered with when it is vitiated by ignoring vital evidence bearing on the issue and by basing the conclusion on oral evidence alone. The supplied judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.second_appeal_in_possession_injunction_s: The proceeding is a second appeal arising from a suit seeking an injunction based on claimed possession.
predicates.vital_documents_ignored: The court whose finding is challenged failed to consider documents that materially bear on possession.
predicates.finding_based_on_oral_evidence_alone: The finding on possession rested on oral evidence without accounting for the material documentary evidence.
predicates.interference_with_vitiated_possession_fi: A finding of possession affected by those evidentiary omissions may be disturbed in second appeal.

issues.definition: When a second appeal in a possession-based injunction suit challenges a finding made without considering vital documents and based on oral evidence alone, that finding may be disturbed.
